- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for volatility drag.
- Model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.3); apply +1.5–2.5% upward adjustment for low sentiment periods.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “1.00” (strong bullish) followed by “0.00” (neutral), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% in next 7-day forecast to reflect sentiment decay.
- In 30-day forecasts, model frequently misses late-period reversals (e.g., 28–30 days); add 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment turns negative in last 3–5 days.
